script.title: Why Do We Itch?
script.hook: Your skin sounds a tiny alarm — and your brain demands you scratch it.

scenes.image_prompt: Bolt freezes mid-flinch with one stubby arm raised just before scratching a forearm resting on a wooden kitchen table in golden evening light, where a single yellow spark of irritation glows on warm coral skin beside a tiny bell-shaped alarm bud popping up from the surface. Off-center, subject lower-right, shallow depth, implied flinch motion. The yellow spark is the hero.

scenes.narration: Every itch is a tiny alarm your skin sets off. Why?
scenes.image_prompt: Bolt yanks a tripwire taut across warm coral skin in a low ground-level cutaway, the wire snapping a yellow alarm spark to life where a speck of dust lands. The surprising element: a brass tripwire trigger threaded through the skin ridge. Foreground blurred skin ridge, midground glowing yellow trigger, background fading coral depth. Asymmetrical, focal yellow upper-right, implied rising pulse.
scenes.text_sub: Your skin just called for help.

scenes.narration: Special skin cells called mast cells respond by dumping a chemical: histamine.
scenes.image_prompt: Bolt cranks open a tiny round mast-cell hatch in an overhead skin cutaway, releasing an orange histamine cloud puffing out across warm coral skin. The surprise: a popped cork flying off the cell like a champagne bottle. Foreground rounded cells, midground orange release hero left-of-center, background soft coral gradient, implied outward burst.

scenes.narration: That histamine docks onto itch nerve endings, firing a signal straight up your spinal cord.
scenes.image_prompt: Bolt grips an electric-blue nerve ending like a doorknob as the orange histamine cloud docks into it, lighting the wire up a diagonal climb through warm coral skin toward the spinal cord. The surprise: a key-shaped histamine molecule slotting into a nerve keyhole. Foreground orange cloud lower-left, midground bright blue nerve, strong diagonal upward zip.
scenes.text_sub: A signal races to the brain.

scenes.narration: Your brain's somatosensory cortex reads the alarm and demands one thing: scratch.
scenes.image_prompt: Bolt slams an alarm lever inside a simplified electric-blue brain cutaway as the nerve signal arrives, a yellow spark flaring in the somatosensory cortex. The surprise: a big red emergency button labeled only by its mushroom shape, half-pressed. Foreground blue nerve entering, midground glowing blue brain hero left, implied pulse-flash.

scenes.narration: Scratching fires faster pain-touch nerves that drown out the itch signal — instant relief.
scenes.image_prompt: Bolt drags a faster orange nerve cable over the itch line on a warm coral forearm, green relief washing over the skin as the new signal overrides the old. The surprise: a green firehose flooding over a smaller yellow alarm, dousing it. Foreground blurred sofa cushion, midground scratching arm, implied override stroke.

scenes.narration: Here's the trick: scratching works by replacing the itch with mild pain your brain prefers.
scenes.image_prompt: Bolt lifts a green relief blanket off warm coral skin to reveal a small red sting of mild pain hiding beneath it, recoiling in shock. The surprise: a red thorn tucked under the green calm layer. Foreground green calm peeling back, midground hidden red pain hero lower-right, implied flicker between green and red.

scenes.narration: But that scratching damages skin, making mast cells dump MORE histamine — itch gets worse.
scenes.image_prompt: Bolt shrinks back from an overhead skin cutaway scraped into a raw red damage patch, fresh orange histamine erupting from the wound as mast-cell hatches fly open again. The surprise: a spinning vault wheel cranking the cycle wider. Foreground red damaged skin, midground new orange clouds, background yellow sparks reigniting, implied spiral repeat.

scenes.narration: So don't scratch — but it's already too late, right?
scenes.image_prompt: Bolt freezes mid-flinch with one stubby arm raised just before scratching a forearm on the same wooden kitchen table in golden evening light, a single yellow spark glowing again on warm coral skin beside the same bell-shaped alarm bud popping up. Off-center, subject lower-right, implied flinch motion identical to scene one.

short_grade.notes: The alarm/tripwire conceit is strong and consistent — tighten scenes 4/7/8 which all sit at 5.0s and risk dragging the back half.
